questions.label: Q1
questions.text: Use two iterations of Newton’s method to estimate the positive root of $x^2 - 3 = 0$, starting your iteration with $x_0 = 2$.
questions.modelAnswer:
For $f(x)=x^2-3$,

$$
x_{n+1}=x_n-\frac{x_n^2-3}{2x_n}=\frac{1}{2}\left(x_n+\frac{3}{x_n}\right).
$$

Starting with $x_0=2$:

$$
x_1=\frac{1}{2}\left(2+\frac{3}{2}\right)=1.75.
$$

$$
x_2=\frac{1}{2}\left(1.75+\frac{3}{1.75}\right)=1.732142857\ldots
$$

The estimate after two iterations is $1.732143$.

questions.label: Q2
questions.text:
Compute the values $z_1 = s''(1)$ and $z_2 = s''(2)$ for the cubic spline $s(x)$ interpolating the data

| x | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| y | 2 | 5 | 4 | 8 |

using the natural spline boundary conditions $s''(0) = s''(3) = 0$. Write down the polynomial $s_1(x)$ giving the values of $s$ for $1 \leq x \leq 2$.

questions.label: Q3
questions.text:
Compute the best linear approximation $l(x)$ in the least-squares sense to the following data:

| x | 1 | 2 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| y | 3 | 2 | 5 | 9 | 7 |

Use $l(x)$ to estimate the value of $y$ when $x = 3$.
questions.modelAnswer:
For $l(x)=a+bx$,

$$
\sum x_i=18, \qquad \sum y_i=26, \qquad \sum x_i^2=82, \qquad \sum x_i y_i=114.
$$

The slope is

$$
b=\frac{5(114)-18(26)}{5(82)-18^2}=\frac{102}{86}=\frac{51}{43}.
$$

The intercept is

$$
a=\frac{26-b(18)}{5}=\frac{40}{43}.
$$

Therefore

$$
l(x)=\frac{40}{43}+\frac{51}{43}x.
$$

At $x=3$,

$$
l(3)=\frac{193}{43}=4.488372\ldots
$$

The estimated value is $y \approx 4.488$.

questions.label: Q7
questions.text:
Compute the Romburg estimate $R_{4,4}$ to the definite integral

$$
\int_0^5 \frac{\sin(x)}{x}\,dx.
$$

Write out the computed values of $R_{i,j}$ to 6 decimal places.
Note: Use $R_{k,1}$ to denote the estimates obtained by the trapezoidal rule with $2^{k-1}$ subdivisions. Take $\sin(x)/x = 1$ when $x = 0$.

questions.label: Q9
questions.text:
Consider the second-order ordinary differential equation

$$
\ddot{x} + 12\dot{x} + 40x = \cos(\pi t/8); \quad x(0) = 1, \dot{x}(0) = 0.
$$

Show how to express this equation as a system of first-order equations, and write down a Matlab function $f(t,X)$ expressing the right-hand side of this system.
Compute the solution of the equation at time $t = 300$ using the builtin Matlab functions ode45 and ode15s. Compare the properties of the two methods, both in terms of the number of steps taken, and the accuracy obtained. Which method is better for this problem? Explain your answer.
Note: The exact solution has $x(300) = -0.002927$ to 6 decimal places.
questions.modelAnswer:
Let

$$
X_1=x, \qquad X_2=\dot{x}.
$$

Then

$$
\dot{X}_1=X_2,
$$

$$
\dot{X}_2=\cos(\pi t/8)-12X_2-40X_1.
$$

A Matlab function for the right-hand side is

```matlab
function dX = f(t,X)
dX = zeros(2,1);
dX(1) = X(2);
dX(2) = cos(pi*t/8) - 12*X(2) - 40*X(1);
end
```

The computation can be performed using

```matlab
[t45,X45] = ode45(@f,[0 300],[1;0]);
[t15,X15] = ode15s(@f,[0 300],[1;0]);

x45 = X45(end,1)
x15 = X15(end,1)
steps45 = length(t45)-1
steps15 = length(t15)-1
err45 = abs(x45 - (-0.002927))
err15 = abs(x15 - (-0.002927))
```

The homogeneous equation has characteristic equation

$$
\lambda^2+12\lambda+40=0,
$$

so

$$
\lambda=-6\pm 2i.
$$

The transient part decays quickly compared with the long interval $0 \leq t \leq 300$, while the forcing term varies slowly. This makes the problem stiff in practice: an explicit solver such as `ode45` is restricted by the rapidly decaying modes and normally takes many more steps. The stiff solver `ode15s` can take larger steps after the transient has decayed and should give a value close to

$$
x(300)=-0.002927.
$$

Thus `ode15s` is the better method for this problem, because it should require fewer steps while retaining comparable or better accuracy at $t=300$.
